subject.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane

question: Should Active Memory recall use per-agent lanes by default, or should cross-agent recall parallelism be gated behind an explicit concurrency/config design?
rationale: The code change is narrow and source-backed, but it intentionally increases possible simultaneous embedded recall work on multi-agent gateways, which is an availability/default policy choice green CI cannot settle.

options.title: Prove and land per-agent default
options.body: Ask for inspectable redacted multi-agent logs or terminal output, then land the PR if the proof shows separate lane keys without shared queue-wait timeouts.

options.title: Require a config-gated design
options.body: Pause this PR and keep the hidden global throttle until the canonical reliability issue defines an explicit Active Memory recall concurrency policy.

options.title: Accept the concurrency risk now
options.body: Maintainers may deliberately land the one-line fix based on source proof and operator reports, while tracking provider/load hardening separately.

recommendation.title: Prove and land per-agent default
recommendation.body: Ask for inspectable redacted multi-agent logs or terminal output, then land the PR if the proof shows separate lane keys without shared queue-wait timeouts.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman introduced the Active Memory plugin and is the strongest feature-history owner for the default recall behavior being changed.
